summary: Abbott said Wednesday it plans to spin out its nutrition business into an independent, publicly traded company. The business has approximately $8.5 billion in annual sales and includes brands like Pedialyte, Similac and Ensure. In Abbott’s third quarter, nutrition brought in revenue of $2.26 billion, representing year-over-year growth of about 5%. Abbott’s nutrition business has been at the center of lawsuits as well as a federal investigation into the manufacturing and handling of a recall of powdered infant formula in 2022 due to potential contamination. In September, the company announced a $385 million settlement with the Department of Justice to resolve claims as well as lawsuits filed by certain relators and the attorneys general in several states.
title: Abbott plans to spin out its nutrition business

summary: Medtronic said Monday it has received a CE mark for its Vitalis portfolio of cardiac pacemakers. The portfolio features five devices, which Medtronic said offer a comprehensive suite of pacing options and include features for conduction system pacing therapy, or CSP. Medtronic named ReSyncra CSP as the most advanced device, highlighting its suitability for use in patients who may benefit from cardiac resynchronization therapy, or CRT, but are failed by traditional approaches to treatment.
title: Medtronic wins CE mark for Vitalis portfolio of cardiac pacemakers

summary: The Food and Drug Administration has cleared the Twiist automated insulin delivery, or AID, system for use in adults with insulin-treated Type 2 diabetes. Sequel Med Tech, which sells the device, disclosed the 510(k) clearance on Friday. The FDA granted the clearance to Deka Research and Development, Sequel’s partner on Twiist. The FDA cleared Twiist after researchers linked the AID system to reduced blood sugar and increased time in the target glycemic range in a clinical trial.
title: FDA clears Sequel’s insulin delivery system in Type 2 diabetes
